thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV2 - gpu-node-47 unreachable (pager: PD#1872) - auto-page fired to eng-oncall. metrics: node-exporter heartbeat missing, kubelet NotReady. link: https://pagerduty.example/PD1872

maria (oncall): acked. I'm on it, pinging infra and support.

ben (eng-sre): seeing alerts too. kubernetes reports Node gpu-node-47 NotReady, last transition ~2026-02-15T02:26:12Z. Could be kernel oops or NVMe panic like last week.

carol (infra): grabbing serial console now. If it's kernel panic we may need an RMA. hardware-bot, can you attach remote-serial?

hardware-bot: remote-serial session started (gpu-node-47). output beginning...

maria (oncall): past few lines from serial:
```
[   12.345678] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception in interrupt
[   12.348901] Call Trace:
[   12.349002]  dump_stack+0x5c/0x8c
[   12.349103]  panic+0x1a3/0x2f0
[   12.349204]  ? gpu_driver_panic+0x1a/0x1a
```

ben (eng-sre): yup, kernel panic. kubelet stuck, that's why we see NotReady. Any pods on that host? check scheduling/status and evict ASAP.

maria (oncall): running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47` now. Found serving-runtime pods + 3 customer jobs (dedicated-tenant A).

maria (oncall): initiating cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-47` -> node cordoned.

maria (oncall): starting drain (ignore daemonsets, delete-local-data for long-running scratch):
```
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

ben (eng-sre): hold - for dedicated customers we need to coordinate with routing. pinging routing to avoid forced fallbacks that might send traffic to slower regions. Also confirm that autoscaler won't try to reschedule heavy GPU pods into undersized nodes.

carol (infra): serial shows NVMe I/O errors before panic. Likely disk/controller fault. Opening RMA ticket: RMA-4557.

dave (support): support notes: two customers (tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma) reported 503s in the last minute on inference endpoints. I'm opening a customer-impact ticket and emailing account reps: "Possible compute host failure impacting dedicated inference. We're routing workloads and will follow up."

maria (oncall): drain completed for most pods, a couple failed to terminate (stuck in Terminating, eviction blocked by volume). Forcing deletion for non-critical test pods, leaving dedicated-tenant pods for safe migration.

ben (eng-sre): rolling fallback plan: switch dedicated-tenant A to their reserved fallback cluster and start provisioning spare GPU slot in Dedicated pool. Will also enable model variant routing to lower-capacity (quantized) instance for public hosted to keep latency.

maria (oncall): running `kubectl describe node gpu-node-47` -> Kubelet LastErr: "failed to update node status: context deadline exceeded". Not surprising given kernel panic.

carol (infra): physical rack team notified. We're scheduling a reboot attempt with IPMI rescue to capture full logs; if that fails, RMA on NVMe controller.

hardware-bot: IPMI reset performed at 02:28:45Z. Node did not come back to network. Serial shows repeated I/O errors and then silence.

ben (eng-sre): since node won't come up, marking impact: 2 tenants affected with degraded throughput, hosted customers experienced transient 503s routed around via cache for ~45s. No data corruption reported.

dave (support): logged customer-impact tickets: INC-9932 (tenant-alpha), INC-9933 (tenant-gamma). Notifying SL representatives.

maria (oncall): escalation: hardware team to handle RMA-4557, infra to remove node from inventory once RMA accepted, eng-sre to re-balance serving groups. I'm switching PagerDuty to "hardware" schedule for follow-up.

carol (infra): creating follow-up runbook notes in incident tracker. Actions: 1) RMA NVMe controller 2) reprovision spare GPU host 3) restore kubelet drain/cordon state on replacement.

ben (eng-sre): post-incident checklist: add kernel oops signature to alerting (pattern match for "kernel panic - not syncing"), add automated pre-drain for nodes with NVMe SMART errors, and confirm Dedicated failover playbook works end-to-end with tenant failover.

maria (oncall): updating incident summary in thread and marking current hands-off to hardware team. Leaving this thread open until RMA confirmed.

hardware-bot: RMA created: RMA-4557, ETA parts 48-72h.

dave (support): I'll follow up with the two tenants with a short postmortem note and ETA.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. If anything changes (node comes back, or more tenants affected) reply here and I'll re-open oncall. :white_check_mark:
